ashby:conveo:435642e1-5925-42e2-9f46-d4f.summary: Conveo is building AI powered consumer understanding infrastructure platform enabling fast, affordable, and high quality consumer / B2B research. Global brands like Unilever, Google, and Orange use our AI video interviewer to generate insights across marketing, product, and research teams.

sections.title: Why this role shapes the whole company
paras: Positioning sits upstream of everything a company says. The words chosen for a segment decide which ads work, which pages convert, which deals open, and which category the market files us under. At most companies that thinking is scattered across founders, sales decks, and agencies. Here it has one owner. You.

Conveo is going from tool to infrastructure, and founding a category to do it. Categories are won inside the buyer's head, which makes the person who truly understands those buyers, and can tell their story back to them better than they can tell it themselves, one of the highest-leverage people in the company. What you write becomes what sales says, what the website claims, what the ads promise, and eventually what the market believes.

This is a whole-company seat. You are the resident empath for everyone who buys Conveo, from the insights leader who runs the platform to the CMO who signs for the infrastructure. Product asks you how a feature should be framed. Sales asks you what to say in the room. Founders ask you whether the narrative holds. When someone anywhere in the company needs to know what our buyers think, want, fear, or say, they come to you, and you know.

sections.title: 1. Understand our buyers better than anyone in the company
paras: Confidence here comes from doing the work, and you know how the work is done.
bullets: Run the positioning exercises: the interviews, win/loss reviews, and segmentation work that establish who buys Conveo, why, and why now
Know where the information lives and go get it: sales calls, transcripts, closed and churned deals, communities, analysts, the product itself
Become an absolute empath for every buyer, from the insights leader to the CMO. Understand their world, their pressures, and their language, and speak it fluently
Keep the buyer map current, so the company's picture of who it serves is always the real one

sections.title: 2. Turn understanding into positioning and narrative. The science and the art
paras: Great product marketing takes both halves, and most people bring one.
bullets: The science: you know the frameworks, the steps, and the deliverables cold. Positioning documents, messaging hierarchies, and proof points built rigorously enough to survive contact with sales
The art: clear taste. Copy that is short, dense, and specific. A narrative that is genuinely compelling. You are an exceptional storyteller, and it shows in everything from a headline to a keynote

sections.title: 3. Take it end to end, with AI
paras: You carry an idea from insight to live page yourself, with AI in every step of the workflow.
bullets: Go from positioning document to finished landing page with your own hands: the hero, the story, the proof, the call to action
Build with AI as a genuine collaborator: research synthesis, drafting, variant production, page assembly. Your output looks like a team's

Teach the AI's. We have multiple agents that do work across a wide array of things. You know how to communicate with these agents such that they can create leverage for everyone from Sales to Customer Success
Own launches from narrative through enablement to measured pipeline, and ship the derivative pack so one piece of thinking becomes a month of distribution
Write the internal artefacts that actually get used: the one pager, the objection handling, the demo narrative, the competitive angle

ashby:docker:66714d32-47cb-4dea-8447-185.summary: Docker is the platform at the center of how intelligent software gets built. For more than a decade, Docker has helped millions of developers and thousands of organizations build, ship, and run software consistently across any environment. Today, Docker extends that same trust to the AI era. Docker Hardened Images form the foundation agentic code is built on, local and cloud Docker Sandboxes isolate where agents run, and Docker AI Governance sets enterprise-wide policy. Together, they give builders and organizations the confidence to adopt any model, tool, or agent without compromising security, governance, or control.

sections.title: The Role
paras: The Products Team at Docker is looking for a Principal Product Manager to lead components of Docker Sandboxes. You will own and drive this strategic product area from high-level concept design through delivery, adoption, and operation. You will help shape how developers and AI agents use fast, secure, isolated environments across local and cloud workflows. You will work closely with developers inside and outside of Docker, our customers, and our partners to expand our open ecosystem offering and provide value. As the company and ecosystem grow, you will help foster teams eager to continuously build, measure, and learn.

To thrive in this role, you will need experience working with developers, deep technical fluency in systems and developer infrastructure, and prior experience as a software engineer. You will need to understand containers, sandboxes/microVMs, virtualization technologies, hypervisors, the software development lifecycle, and how untrusted or agent-generated code can be safely executed and orchestrated. You will need a relentless drive to try new things and an eye for detail. Your long-term success will depend on your ability to own the product roadmap, earn the trust of the developer community, and scale reliable services. Most importantly, you will need to be comfortable taking ownership of big objectives with big goals, working with a cross-functional team, and maintaining a bias for action.

sections.title: Responsibilities
bullets: You own Docker Sandboxes, its long-term vision, roadmap, revenue, adoption, and results.

You believe in and can succinctly articulate our customers, their workflows, and their pain points. You empathize with the world they live in and the security, performance, compatibility, and cost constraints they work through.

You will engage deeply with developers building AI agents, coding environments, CI and testing systems, and other workloads that require secure, isolated execution, finding solutions for today while optimizing for tomorrow's vision.

You enjoy building infrastructure products that are easy to adopt and use. You will turn complex tradeoffs across isolation, startup time, performance, density, networking, storage, and cost into simple product experiences.
You are comfortable with ambiguity and will guide product definition, feature prioritization, and scope in concert with engineering, design, security, operations, and go-to-market teams.
You are a fan of iterative development, working with customers and cross-functional teams to hypothesize, measure adoption and impact, learn from releases, and continually improve the roadmap.

sections.title: Qualifications
bullets: You have deep empathy for the needs of developers and are obsessed with talking to your users.
You have prior professional experience as a software engineer, ideally in systems, infrastructure, platform engineering, developer tools, or cloud.
You have strong technical familiarity with sandboxes/microVMs, containers, virtualization technologies, and hypervisors, including the isolation and security boundaries each provides.
You understand the building blocks of modern developer infrastructure, including Linux, container runtimes, orchestration, networking, storage, APIs, and cloud services.
You have experience designing, building, or operating systems that execute customer-provided, untrusted, or agent-generated code at scale.
You are comfortable interacting with a command-line interface and discussing APIs, SDKs, and technical architecture with engineers and developers.
You have experience building B2B or SaaS products, or a background in public cloud and developer infrastructure.
You understand software supply chain and software security concerns, including multi-tenant isolation, identity, secrets management, observability, and reliability.

ashby:flai:2946b0c2-d769-4a72-a7c3-9fdb1.summary:
AI has transformed B2B SaaS, but it has struggled to reach the real-world industries that shape our lives. Flai is building the leading AI-native service CRM for car dealerships.

Auto dealerships are a $1.3 trillion industry and sell 96% of the 16 million new cars sold each year. Yet they still run on outdated systems and manual processes, and they spend $36B a year on operations. That’s our opportunity.

In August 2026, Prefect and Dagster, competitors for eight years, joined forces to build the next generation of automation infrastructure. Today, our ecosystem includes Dagster, the data platform; Prefect, the agent platform; and FastMCP, the leading open-source developer framework for the MCP ecosystem. Together, our open-source and commercial products are trusted by Fortune 500 companies, data innovators, and high-growth technology companies around the world.

sections.title: About Prefect
paras: We think of our culture as the operating system of the company. We’ve carefully created a supportive, high-performance environment that empowers our team to do the best work of their careers, have meaningful impact, and continue growing personally and professionally. We’re a remote-first team that values high standards, ownership, and thoughtful collaboration.

sections.title: Role Summary:
paras: Prefect acquired Dagster this summer. Our sales engineers now sell three things. Prefect Cloud. Dagster+. And the next generation of AI tooling we're building across both: governed access to tools and data for agents, and durable workflows where agents and humans do the work together.

We're also selling something that isn't on a pricing page. FastMCP, our open-source MCP framework, sits inside a lot of production agent stacks, so teams come to us for how the whole thing should fit: the data layer, the orchestration layer, the context layer, and how agents and humans operate across all three. Much of what a sales engineer does here is demonstrate the art of the possible.

You're a Senior Sales Engineer on the Prefect subject-matter-expert pod, reporting to Wayne Grigsby, Sales Engineering Lead. The pod sits alongside our Dagster pod, and both roll up to Director of Sales Engineering, who runs the function end to end, pre-sale and post-sale.

sections.title: What You'll Do:
bullets: Own the technical side of enterprise deals. F rom discovery through close: advising prospects, presenting and demonstrating the value of our platforms from a technical perspective.

Distill the use case. Most prospects don't arrive with a clean requirement. They arrive with a data platform, a pile of tools, a team of engineers and users expecting answers, and a budget. You figure out how our products fit together to solve for their use case, then help them validate the approach.

Sell across the platform. A single conversation can span Prefect, Dagster, FastMCP, hybrid architecture, and AI governance, often with a team that knows where it wants to end up but not how to get there.

Turn field signal into product direction. Sales engineers are the closest thing to a market pulse this company has. You'll carry what you hear into our GTM-engineering partnership channels, with evidence, and push when it matters.
Build the things we sell with. Demo environments, architecture diagrams, competitive battlecards, contributions to our internal repos, personal projects, and the occasional blog post.
Contribute and advocate for your ideas . Champion the culture, and keep projects from quietly failing. When something is going sideways, you say so early and you help fix it.

sections.title: Your Qualifications:
paras: Five things. If you have these, apply, even if the nice-to-haves are thin.
bullets: 3+ years of engineering experience, building real solutions. Data engineering, DevOps, software engineering, data science: the discipline matters less than the fact that you've built something programmatically and shipped it. Python is our house language.

2+ years in a customer facing role. Deep discovery skills and the habit of uncovering the real problem before proposing anything is key. You ask the second and third question, and you notice what the customer isn't saying.

Curiosity first, then creativity. You take things apart to see how they work, and you don't stop at the docs. Then you put the pieces together in ways nobody handed you: a new use case, a demo that didn't exist yesterday, a workaround the customer didn't know was possible.
You explain hard things clearly to engineers. What's required is that a senior platform engineer finishes a call with you and trusts you.

sections.title: About the role
paras: There are close to a billion knowledge workers in the world, and only a small fraction of them have worked with AI that makes them better at what they do. In the enterprise, reaching the rest depends on the IT, security, and business leaders who decide whether to adopt AI, and the admins who decide how it's deployed, governed, and scaled across their organizations. They ask hard questions before they say yes, and this role owns how we answer them.

We're looking for a Product Marketing Manager to own positioning for Claude's core knowledge-work products (Chat, Cowork, and the broader non-coding suite) for enterprise decision makers and admins. You'll work across the areas that matter most to enterprise customers today: security and observability, workspace management and deployment controls, and pricing and packaging. You'll own the materials that help a decision maker or admin understand what's possible, roll Claude out with confidence, and make the case internally, including product launches, the website, pitch decks, battlecards, persona narratives, pricing and packaging story, and admin communications. Beyond making the case for adopting AI, you'll help the people accountable for deploying it do that safely, and show them exactly how to put it to work across their organizations.

This is an individual-contributor role for someone who loves the hands-on work of product marketing, on products with enormous, established usage and a fast launch cadence. You'll write the positioning doc, build the battlecard, and ship the persona work yourself, and you'll use Claude to keep it all current, so the teams that depend on it can trust it.

sections.title: Key responsibilities
bullets: Define the story that earns enterprise trust. Own the positioning and messaging house for Chat, Cowork, and Claude's core knowledge-work products for admins, so every deck, campaign, and piece of content makes the same case for adopting and scaling Claude.

Own the story for how enterprises run Claude. Lead positioning and launches across security and observability, workspace management, and the controls for managing deployments, working with Product to turn new capabilities into clear reasons to adopt and expand.

Give sellers the conviction to close. Build and maintain the sales enablement assets (pitch decks, battle cards, objection handling) that help GTM answer security, deployment, and pricing questions with confidence.

Help decision makers and admins make the call. Own the proof points, comparisons, and narratives that help decision makers, admins, and their IT and security teams evaluate Claude and justify the investment and rollout internally.

Make our pricing and packaging easy to understand and buy. Partner with Product, Finance, and GTM on how we present plans, pricing, and packaging for Claude Enterprise, and build the cost and value story that helps customers make the case to scale.

Make sure the message reaches the right person, in their language. Develop ICP and persona frameworks that cover a varied base of enterprise decision makers and admins (executive buyers, IT, security, compliance, and workspace owners) in enough detail to shape messaging and campaigns for each one.

Make our website answer buyers' questions. Own the website and product page messaging for Claude Enterprise, including how we present admin controls, security, governance, and plans and pricing. It's often where a buyer or admin decides whether to take a closer look.

Turn scattered wins into a playbook others can run. Build libraries of top enterprise deployment and admin use cases by product and by function or industry, so the best examples of successful rollouts become patterns anyone can copy.

greenhouse:dorsia:5256835007.summary:
Dorsia is an AI-native hospitality-tech company redefining access to the world's most coveted tables, events, and cultural moments. We give our members exclusive access and our operators unmatched control, visibility, and revenue.

We don't just provide access, we create it. Dorsia owns its luxury experiential events end-to-end, from the guest list to production and the technology behind every entrance. Through our enterprise platform, we're building the infrastructure layer for the future of hospitality, powering leading hotels and private member clubs with the same systems that run Dorsia.

We grew 480% in 2025 and today we operate across 400+ venues in 26 cities with revenue engines spanning consumer and enterprise membership, Dorsia Pay, the Culture Calendar, and our enterprise platform.

sections.title: About the Role
paras: Dorsia is seeking a Product Manager, Payments to own Dorsia Pay and the full member payment experience, from card on file and deposits through checkout, split bills, tipping, settlement, and post-dining support. At Dorsia, the best payment is the one a member never has to think about. We're getting there with agents that understand intent, use payment tools, act within clear permissions, recover from exceptions, and move real money on a member's behalf. The hardest problem in agentic commerce is trust, and this role owns it.

This is a builder role at the boundary of product, engineering, and operations. You won't just write requirements for AI features or bolt on off-the-shelf copilots. You'll prototype agents yourself, define their tools and decision boundaries, write the evals, read the traces, and decide how much autonomy they've earned before they reach production.

The right candidate has hands-on experience in consumer payments or digital wallets, has shipped payment features on mobile, and has built and deployed agents that take real actions in production, beyond features that only summarize or suggest. You'll be accountable for payment conversion, adoption, authorization rates, agent task completion, member trust, and operational leverage.

sections.title: Product Strategy and Execution
bullets: Shape the roadmap for Dorsia Pay and the in-app wallet, with agentic payments at the core.
Build and ship agents that settle checks, handle deposits and tipping, and recover failed payments on members' behalf.
Define each agent's tools, context, permissions, and escalation paths, with hard limits on amount, risk, and reversibility.
Prototype agent behaviors in code, get them in front of users in days, and partner with engineering to ship what works.
Build golden task sets and adversarial evals before launch, inspect production traces, and expand autonomy only when the evidence earns it.

sections.title: Payment Experience and Design Flow
bullets: Audit and optimize core payment flows, from card onboarding and Apple Pay through split bills, tipping, and post-dining support.
Replace multi-screen workflows with intent, so a member can split a bill, add a guest, or fix a charge with a single request.
Design for delegation, so members can hand a payment job to an agent and trust the outcome.
Build confirmation, explanation, rollback, and human-handoff patterns for ambiguous or high-stakes actions.
Turn wireframes and agent behaviors into testable builds in days, then refine them through live traces and usability testing.

sections.title: Payments Infrastructure and Partnerships
bullets: Partner with engineering and finance on processor integrations, tokenization, venue payouts, ledgers, and reconciliation.
Help build a reusable agentic payments platform with shared tools, policies, evals, and observability.
Deploy back-office agents for reconciliation, disputes, fraud triage, and payout exceptions as volume scales.
Turn operators' repeated judgment calls into safe, testable agent capabilities.
Partner with risk, legal, and compliance to define the controls, audit trails, and scoped permissions for agent-initiated transactions.

As an Account Manager, Client Development & Renewals, you will be tasked with owning a book of existing customer accounts and driving both renewal retention and expansion revenue within them. This is not a transactional renewals seat; it is a growth-first role where renewal is the floor, not the goal, and you will protect the base by keeping renewals healthy and on time and grow it by uncovering and closing whitespace, running consultative upsell and cross-sell conversations, and turning satisfied customers into expanding ones. You will sit within the Client Development / Renewals organization and partner closely with Account Executives, Customer Success Managers, and Sales Engineering, in a role built for a rep who is driven to outgrow a base they know well, own their numbers, and earn a path to strategic accounts or AE-track roles through expansion results.

sections.title: What Will You Do?
bullets: Identify churn and downgrade risk early by watching deployment health, usage, support signals, and sentiment across your accounts; run save motions on at-risk accounts, pulling in CSM, Support, and leadership when needed; flag overdeployment/downgrade exposure and get ahead of it before it hits the renewal.

Own an accurate, transparent forecast across both renewal and expansion pipeline for your book; keep Salesforce and CPQ/quoting tools current, with accurate stages and a renewal/expansion pipeline you can defend; structure and close deals cleanly, using approved pricing and quote automation.

sections.title: What Skills and Knowledge Will You Bring?
bullets: 3 to 5 years in renewals, account management, or a customer-facing sales role, with upsell/cross-sell closing experience on your record, ideally in SaaS or cybersecurity.
A track record of hitting or beating quota, including driving net revenue retention above 100 percent on your own book (expansion outpacing churn), not just renewal completion.
Proven experience running consultative upsell/cross-sell motions and identifying and closing whitespace within an existing customer base.
Comfort managing multi-stakeholder conversations and negotiations, with direct experience negotiating with senior/economic buyers.
A risk-aware instinct: you notice the early signals of churn or downgrade and act before renewal time.
Strong forecasting discipline and CRM hygiene; hands-on with Salesforce and CPQ/quote tools.
Strong communication and organization, curiosity about customer use-cases and the product, and a habit of opening expansion conversations without being prompted.
Exposure to Channel/MSSP or 2-tier GTM models is a plus, not a requirement.

greenhouse:stripe:8384438.summary: Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies, from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups, use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

sections.title: About the team
paras: The Consumer Bank Network team helps people do more with their bank accounts. We build consumer experiences for connecting financial accounts and making payments across Stripe, spanning Financial Connections and Link . We make these experiences simple, secure, and trustworthy.

The team owns the user experience for one of the highest-traffic products at Stripe. Our work spans onboarding, authentication, checkout, and returning user experiences. We combine product design, experimentation, and personalization to reduce friction, improve conversion, and help consumers discover and adopt payment methods that meet their needs. For businesses, this means easier customer onboarding and better payment experiences. This is both an application and platform team: in addition to the thousands of merchants integrating the Financial Connections UX, more than a dozen teams across Stripe also rely on Financial Connections to serve their users.

Link is used by more than 300 million consumers . You’ll build consumer experiences within that ecosystem, where small improvements in conversion can help more people connect accounts, make purchases, and get paid.

sections.title: What you’ll do
paras: You’ll own the strategy and roadmap for consumer growth, conversion, and payment method adoption across Financial Connections and Link. You’ll work across the consumer journey, from connecting a financial account to completing a purchase, setting up a subscription, managing your finances with your agent of choice, or receiving a payout.

This role combines a high bar for consumer product craft with a disciplined approach to growth. You’ll turn user research and funnel analysis into ideas, work closely with Engineering, Design, and Data Science to test them, and scale what works. You’ll shape both the everyday details of the experience and larger changes to how people discover and use financial products.

sections.title: Responsibilities
bullets: Set the product strategy and priorities for consumer conversion, growth, and payment method adoption across Financial Connections and Link.

Build a steady pipeline of experiments, from targeted UX improvements to new growth opportunities. Define hypotheses, success measures, and guardrails, then use results to decide what to ship, change, or stop.
Partner closely with Design and User Research to understand consumer behavior and create clear, intuitive experiences across consent, authentication, bank selection, and error recovery.

Partner with Engineering and Data Science to build personalized consumer experiences using machine learning and adaptive experimentation, improving conversion and payment method adoption while balancing user value, business outcomes, and consumer trust.
Own measurement of conversion, activation, and payment method adoption. Understand differences across consumer cohorts and use cases, and distinguish product impact from changes in traffic mix.
Work with Engineering to improve reliability and experience quality, resolve friction, and make it easier to deliver and evaluate product changes.

Lead work across Link, Payments, Financial Connections, and cross-functional teams such as Partnerships, Risk, and Legal. Address important merchant needs while keeping the team focused on its highest-impact opportunities.
Be the face of the product for Stripe’s users and external partners, showcasing and building demos and prototypes in collaboration with Engineering, Design, and Go-to-Market teams.
